doc.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Boston, Berklee and New York encounters
title: Miles's rhythm section and Coltrane before his change
summary: The Chambers, Garland and Philly Joe section and early Coltrane, who sounded like Sonny Stitt.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Yeah, he played … you know, played well, just like everybody else. Actually, I liked, I liked … the first time when I was here, Miles‟ group was Paul Chambers and Red Garland, uh, Philly Joe [Jones]. That was something. I really thought it was … that was like a modern, what do you call, Basie‟s famous, you know, rhythm section, except no guitar player. But uh, it was really fantastic.
Was Coltrane in the group, too?

First Coltrane, then it was a short while, he was replaced by Sonny Rollins. He was there briefly, then Coltrane [came] back. But before Coltrane, after he [got] back he would sit in a lot, and that‟s what the people know [as] Coltrane today. But the first Coltrane, when I heard, he was a little more like Sonny Stitt, kind of like that. Except he had his own little voice, you know; I mean his tone was a little bit different. But he was kind of a Sonny Stitt-type of player.
